rows.what_the_ink_shows: The equivalence statement ends with a double-underlined n≥2. The next parenthesis visibly reads “mais non si n=2”; its final numeral has the upper curve, diagonal descent, and horizontal foot of 2, not a single upright 1. Both duplicate correction rows concern this same place. Inspected the full scan and crops/72_scan017_L0_equivalence.jpg and crops/72_scan017_L109_parenthesis.jpg.
rows.note: Written: equivalence of categories si n≥2, followed by “mais non si n=2”. Intended reading supplied by the row: “mais non si n=1”. The manuscript itself supplies the conflicting 2, so this is the author’s slip rather than a transcription misreading. Leave unchanged. References to the margin of 72/76, the lemma of 72/95, and uniqueness of lifting in rank≥3 are carried as supplied background; those other pages were not inspected and the theorem was not independently proved.
rows.event_type: used and rechecked in this run
rows.event_outcome: Visual comparison confirmed the literal final 2 in the parenthesis and the preceding n≥2. No independent check of the cited cross-page evidence or proof of the lifting assertion.
